short: STAR: tell me about a hard bug
question: Tell me about a hard bug you fixed.

scenes.sub: Situation, Task, Action, Result. Pick your own real story; these are examples.
scenes.say: Tell me about a hard bug. Use the S T A R method. The stories here are made-up examples. In your interview, use a real one of your own.

scenes.head: Tell it like a story to a friend

items.label: Situation
items.sub: A file manager froze on folders with 50,000 files

items.label: Task
items.sub: Own the fix: open a folder in under a second

items.label: Action
items.sub: Profiled it, found a re-sort on every insert, batched

items.label: Result
items.sub: From seconds to under one second, plus a test

scenes.say: Tell it like a story to a friend. Situation: where are we? A desktop file manager froze on folders with fifty thousand files. Task: what was my job? Own the fix, under a second. Action: what did I do? Profiled, found a re-sort on every insert, batched it. Result: seconds down to under one, plus a test.

scenes.head: The action: name the real cause
scenes.say: Keep the technical part short and specific. Before: every insert triggered a sort, so fifty thousand inserts meant fifty thousand sorts. After: add everything, then sort once. This is a sketch, in the style of a Q T app in C plus plus. Naming the real cause is what impresses, not just saying it was slow.

scenes.head: Example two: a flaky score in a web app

items.sub: read, add, write lost an update

scenes.say: Second example. Symptom: a web app showed a wrong score, only sometimes. I reproduced it by sending requests in parallel. Root cause: two requests read the same score, each added points, and one write overwrote the other. The fix was one atomic update in the database. And to prevent it, a concurrency test.

scenes.head: In the interview: follow-ups
rows: Add monitoring earlier, so I'd catch it sooner.
How did you know it was fixed?
A before and after measurement, plus a test.
Say what you did, by name: I profiled, I wrote the fix.
Long background, saying we, and no result.
scenes.say: Likely follow-ups. What would you do differently? Name one real improvement. How did you know it was fixed? A measurement, plus a test. Was it a team effort? Say what you did, by name. The common mistake: a long background, saying we, and no result.

lines: Situation, task, action, result, in order, about ninety seconds.
I name the real root cause and use I, not we.
I end with a number and one lesson.
scenes.say: Situation, task, action, result, in order, about ninety seconds. I name the real root cause and say I, not we. I end with a number and one lesson.
